name: Keycloak JWT verifier
purpose: The verifier the mechanism uses when the realm record's `verificationMode` is `jwks`. Owns the JWKS fetch cache with kid-miss refresh, the signature check, the standard-claims validation, and the extraction of the verified claim record the role adapter reads. Does NOT own the token stream (that is the flow controller in the sibling blueprints' vocabulary, delegated here to a project-side authorisation-code state machine that a project either authors above this blueprint or draws from the vendor-neutral sibling if composed).
responsibilities: Fetch and cache the realm's JWKS by realmSlug; TTL is the record's `jwksCacheTtlSeconds` (default 900); refresh from the head of the cache queue at expiry (AC-11103-1).

Verify signature against a key resolved by `kid`; on a kid-miss trigger exactly one JWKS refresh; refuse the token with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_KID_UNKNOWN` when the refresh does not surface the kid (AC-11103-2).

Validate the standard claim set: `iss` equals the record's discovered issuer; `aud` contains the record's `clientId` OR `azp` equals it; `exp` in the future by at least one second; `nbf` not in the future; `iat` in the past by no more than `idTokenMaxAgeSeconds` (AC-11104-1).

Refuse with `KEYCLOAK_JWT_EXPIRED`, `KEYCLOAK_JWT_ISSUER_MISMATCH`, `KEYCLOAK_JWT_AUDIENCE_MISMATCH`, or `KEYCLOAK_JWT_SIGNATURE_INVALID` per failure class; emit one structured audit event `keycloak.jwt_refused` carrying realmSlug, reasonClass, and no token value (AC-11104-2).

Return the verified claim record `{ sub, email?, azp, iss, aud, exp, iat, resource_access?, realm_access?, plus other realm-declared claims }` to the caller; the caller (the role adapter, the session-bridge in opaque-handle mode, the bearer verifier in stateless mode) consumes from that record (AC-11101-3).
Refuse a JWKS fetch failure at verification time with `KEYCLOAK_JWKS_UNREACHABLE`; the token is refused, not silently trusted (AC-11103-2).
internalStructure: One factory function producing a verify closure over the injected discovery-client (TAC-1201, which exposes the record's discovered endpoints), an injected `httpFetch` port for JWKS, an injected clock, and an injected auditSink. The JWKS cache is a Map keyed by realmSlug whose value is `{ keys[], fetchedAt }`; the crypto is either the process's Web Crypto (Node 20+) or a project-injected primitive.

interfaces.name: discoveryClient
interfaces.description: TAC-1201's exported endpoint-record accessor: `endpoints(realmSlug) -> { issuer, jwksUri, ... }`.

interfaces.name: httpFetch
interfaces.description: Process HTTP-fetch port; shared with the discovery client.

interfaces.name: clock
interfaces.description: Injected time source for TTL and expiry checks.

interfaces.name: auditSink
interfaces.description: Structured-event sink; never invoked with a token value.

tradeoffs: TTL-plus-kid-miss caching is the standard shape for JWKS verification; the trade against a shorter TTL is one background refresh per window; against a longer TTL is a bounded staleness window. Refusing on a kid-miss after one refresh defends against amplification while still recovering from a rotation the realm has published. Fixed refusal codes make failure classes observable in the audit stream without a runtime taxonomy the operator has to learn.
